name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Steady large-cap pharma with a growing pipeline and a reasonable valuation; it holds up when the market falls.
targets.risks: Keytruda's patent expiry later this decade and US drug pricing policy.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Low-cost US steel producer with a strong balance sheet that benefits from tariffs and infrastructure demand.
targets.risks: Steel prices falling if the economy slows.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Permian natural gas gathering and processing; fee-based cash flows and a growing dividend.
targets.risks: Lower Permian drilling activity if oil prices fall.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Leading cybersecurity platform with durable recurring-revenue growth; the acquisitions add AI security features.
targets.risks: Its high valuation is exposed to further selling of growth stocks.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: The simpler post-split DuPont is re-rating on better margins and cash flow; the stock is near its high.
targets.risks: Weak industrial demand and costs from PFAS lawsuits.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Beat on third-quarter earnings, raised its dividend 10% and buys back a lot of stock; refiner margins are still healthy.
targets.risks: Refiner profit margins falling from peak levels.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: Cheap generic drug maker that keeps reaching new highs as its turnaround and buybacks progress.
targets.risks: Generic price pressure and problems at its manufacturing plants.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Efficient refiner that returns a lot of cash to shareholders; strong export and renewable diesel businesses.
targets.risks: The same refiner-margin risk as MPC; together they are a concentrated bet.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth management gives steady fees, and recovering deal-making helps the investment bank.
targets.risks: Weak markets reduce trading and advisory revenue.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Storage demand from AI data work and a shift to flash storage; reasonably valued with good cash flow.
targets.risks: Caught in the hardware selloff ahead of late-November earnings.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Q3 revenue grew 20% and billings guidance was raised for the third time this year; the 37% one-month drop looks like selling with the rest of tech, not a broken company.
targets.risks: Firewall upgrade cycle slowing and the stock staying weak below its 200-day average.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Raised its full-year revenue and earnings forecasts, with strong free cash flow, despite missing on Q3 revenue.
targets.risks: Weak China sales and slower lab spending.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Test and measurement equipment for AI, 6G and defense; it fell with tech without any company news.
targets.risks: Mid-to-late November earnings could confirm slowing orders.

targets.name: Humana
targets.thesis: Much better 2027 Medicare star ratings support earnings recovering from the depressed 2026 base by 2028; a defensive name that doesn't depend on oil prices or AI spending.
targets.risks: Medicare Advantage medical costs rising, or worse government payment rates.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
